strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy special-value bug in the CDFLIB wrapper for `scipy.special._cdflib_wrappers.stdtr`/`stdtrit`: when `df == -np.inf`, the buggy revision applies the generic infinity shortcut (`if isinf(df)`) and returns the “normal” result instead of `NaN`. The fixed revision restricts the shortcut to positive infinity (`if isinf(df) and df > 0`), so `df == -inf` returns `NaN` (triggering the added test).

oracle.why: The evidence shows the fix changes the condition from `if isinf(df)` to `if isinf(df) and df > 0`, which specifically affects whether `df == -inf` is treated as a generic infinity case. The test encodes the expected special-value behavior as all-NaN outputs.

fails_on_buggy.value: `assert np.all(np.isnan(sp.stdtr(-np.inf, [-np.inf, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, np.inf])))` and `assert np.all(np.isnan(sp.stdtrit(-np.inf, [0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0])))` fail because the wrapper incorrectly treats `df == -np.inf` as “infinite” and returns the normal/ndtr-based shortcut result instead of `NaN`.
